messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for sdk-service v3.3.0 -> target 5% traffic to canary-3

Maya: seeing a spike of 5xx on /v1/stream and /v1/paging, started ~10:12 UTC. Streaming sessions truncating.

Maya: quick snippet from canary logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:31Z ERROR stream/handshake.go: handshake failed: unsupported frame-version 4 (expected <=3)
2026-03-15T10:12:33Z WARN paging/decoder.go: cursor decode failed: nonzero-offset(12) != expected 0
trace: conn=canary-3-pod-7a
```

Sam - CS: getting CS tickets from AcmeCorp and BetaApps — Acme: "requests time out or stream truncates". They claim ~50% fail rate.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — INC-20260315-0732 assigned to @Priya (oncall) :rotating_light:

Priya: taking this. thx. Maya can you confirm list of affected endpoints and any host ids?

Maya: affected endpoints: /v1/stream (streaming handshake), /v1/paging (cursor decode). Affected hosts: canary-3-pod-7a, canary-3-pod-8c, canary-3-pod-9f.

Liam: that "unsupported frame-version" looks like the new wire change from client handshake bump in 3.3 — canary servers are rejecting older clients still sending frame-version 3.

Evan: timeline: canary deploy at 10:10 UTC -> errors start 10:12 UTC.

Priya: immediate mitigation options:
1) flip kill flag to stop routing to canary (fast)
2) hotpatch canary to accept legacy frames (fast-ish if flag-controlled)
3) rollback canary images to 3.2 (safe but takes a few mins)
Which do we want?

Maya: kill flag fastest. Router command below:
```
curl -XPOST https://console.internal/flags/kill -d '{"flag":"sdk_canary_3_3_route","value":true}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN"
```

Priya: executing kill flag now.

Priya: (runs command) response: 200 OK. Routing change propagated to edge.

incident-bot: ROUTING FLAG toggled: sdk_canary_3_3_route -> true by Priya at 10:16 UTC :white_check_mark:

Maya: monitoring — errors dropped significantly, but in-flight streams already failed (partial responses). CS reporting some lingering truncated sessions.

Sam - CS: AcmeCorp status: degraded; ~50% streaming sessions failed for the 10:12–10:18 window. They are pinned to SDK 3.1.

Liam: follow-up: why are canary servers rejecting older clients? The server handshake change in PR #4921 enforces strict frame-version. That should've been feature-gated.

Priya: plan: keep kill flag. Medium term: rollback canary nodes to 3.2 image immediately. Long term: make handshake backward-compatible and add interop tests. Can we rollback now?

Evan: yes. Command to rollback canary images:
```
kubectl set image deployment/sdk-service-canary sdk-service=redwood/sdk-service:3.2.0-canary -n production
```

Priya: applying rollback now. Rolling pods terminating and new pods starting.

Maya: after rollback, logs show legacy frames accepted again. Paging decoder errors subsided. Monitoring reports 5xx back to baseline by 10:24 UTC.

incident-bot: CANARY ROLLBACK COMPLETE at 10:25 UTC. Incident severity downgraded to P2.

Sam - CS: AcmeCorp and BetaApps confirm stability restored. Acme requested follow-up timeline.

Priya: preliminary root cause: server handshake strictness merged in v3.3 (PR #4921) accidentally rejected older-frame clients. Also related: paging cursor decoder change (PR #4924) assumed new zero-offset encoding and failed for older cursors.

Maya: both issues together explain streaming truncation and paging decode failures for legacy clients.

Priya: immediate action items:
- revert handshake strictness in release branch (owner: Liam)
- patch paging decoder to support legacy cursor offsets or fallback (owner: Maya)
- add interop e2e CI covering SDK clients 3.1..3.3 (owner: Priya)
- hold aggressive canary auto-rollouts until gated (owner: Platform team)

Liam: opening hotfix PR to accept legacy frames in server handshake and will run expedited integration tests. Target: PR + canary redeploy to 3.3.1 within 30–60m if green.

Priya: customer impact assessment (high-level): 6 customers reported tickets. Top affected: AcmeCorp (SLA 99.9) — impact: truncated streams and 502s during ~10:12–10:24 UTC window. No data lost; primarily availability and partial responses. Recommend CS+Revenue evaluate credit (suggestion: 1 day pro-rata for directly impacted).

Sam - CS: I'll collate affected customer list and draft comms. Will coordinate final wording with Priya and Liam.

Maya: adding telemetry monitor for "handshake_mismatch_count" and paging decode failures; alerting threshold lowered for now.

Evan: good mitigation. Please attach runbook commands and timestamps to INC-20260315-0732.

Priya: assigning postmortem owners. I'll keep this incident open until PR merges and new canary proves stable for 1 hour. Tagging @Liam for follow-up.

Liam: acknowledged. I'll post PR link and CI results here when ready.

Maya: note: we should also audit any config changes that un-gated the strict check — might be an accidental default flip in the release config.

Priya: agreed. Adding config audit to follow-ups. Closing slack thread once PR merged and canary stable. Thanks everyone for quick response. :handshake:
